John also draws constantly on the visions of Daniel the OT prophet in the text of Revelation, & in the apocalyptic tradition that developed in the centuries between those 2 books, any use of the phrase 'one like a son of man' is a deliberate allusion to the 'one like a son of man' in Daniel's vision of the 4 beasts.
In that vision, against the backdrop of the rise of successive beastly human kingdoms (including Rome itself as 'a fourth beast, terrible & dreadful & exceedingly strong'), this 'one like a son of man' comes as a heavenly figure before the Ancient of days to receive 'dominion & glory a&nd kingdom ... an everlasting dominion' (Dan 7:13-14). In this vision (& in the apocalyptic tradition developing in the centuries after it - cf. 1 Enoch 46) the title 'son of man' (despite its apparent emphasis on the humanity of the Person being identified) actually came to have heavenly, transcendent & even divine connotations.
The overall message of Revelation obviously resonates deeply with that vision of Daniel; indeed, John's numerous allusions to Daniel's visions (especially in chapters 7 & 10) indicate that he saw his own visions as continuous with Daniel's, & perhaps as clarifying those earlier visions.
